discovery: Experimental observation of fractional charge and anyonic exchange statistics of quasiparticles in the fractional quantum Hall effect

nominees.name: Moty Heiblum
nominees.affiliation: Weizmann Institute of Science, Rehovot, Israel

nominees.name: Gwendal Fève
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique de l'École Normale Supérieure, Paris, France

subfield: Condensed matter physics (fractional quantum Hall effect, anyons, topological order)
motivation: Laughlin predicted that electrons in the fractional quantum Hall regime form a liquid whose excitations carry a fraction of the electron charge and obey anyonic statistics, neither bosonic nor fermionic. For decades this was a theoretical picture. Heiblum's shot-noise experiments measured fractional charges e/3 and later e/4 directly, and developed the quantum-limited mesoscopic tools that made quasiparticle physics measurable. Manfra's ultra-high-mobility heterostructures and Fabry-Perot interferometers produced clean phase jumps revealing the braiding phase of anyons at nu = 1/3. Fève's anyon collider showed the statistical exchange phase through current correlations. Together they established anyons, a new class of quantum particles existing only in two dimensions, as experimental reality. This changes how we think about quantum statistics itself and opens the path toward topologically protected quantum information, now being extended to non-Abelian states and graphene platforms.
